entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Meeting highlights from the Committee for Veterinary Medicinal Products (CVMP) 6-8 October 2026
entries.description: CVMP opinions on veterinary medicinal productsThe Committee adopted a positive opinion, in exceptional circumstances, for a marketing authorisation for Bovilis Lumpyvax (lumpy…
entries.summary: The CVMP adopted a positive opinion, in exceptional circumstances, for a marketing authorisation of Bovilis Lumpyvax.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams working on veterinary products must prepare to submit a marketing authorisation application for Bovilis Lumpyvax now that it has a positive opinion.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA clarified the PIP compliance verification procedure and paediatric reward framework.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling product registrations must review the updated verification process and ensure they meet PIP compliance and paediatric reward criteria.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: Release of compressed ASCII text files containing the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that the NOC data is now available for download and analysis, enabling them to update compliance records and monitor regulatory changes.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot will become a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: Sponsors preparing clinical trial applications, including RA teams, should note that the guidance service will now be available indefinitely and plan their submission workflows accordingly.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety updates were applied to product monographs for submissions cleared between 01‑09‑2026 and 30‑09‑2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling these submissions must review the updated monographs to ensure compliance with the new brand safety requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance for market authorization holders on how to report drug shortages and discontinuations to comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow the new reporting procedures to meet regulatory requirements for drug shortages and discontinuations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance for drug licence holders on how to distribute Canadian market drugs for consumption or use outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to ensure licence holders comply with export distribution rules as outlined in sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide provides instructions on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs to address shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must use it to comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations when managing drug supply gaps.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs during shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams must follow the new guidance to adjust expiry dates appropriately when drug shortages occur.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new Register of Innovative Drugs has been established, listing drugs pursuant to sub‑section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to verify whether their products are included in the register and ensure ongoing compliance with the associated regulatory requirements.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: EMA provides updated procedural advice for applicants using the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams preparing centralised applications should review the new guidance to ensure compliance with the latest EMA requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: Release of a new Drug Product Database extract containing complete information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical categories.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to access and utilize the updated database to ensure their product listings and regulatory submissions reflect the most current product status and details.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to the product information
entries.description: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to the product information
entries.summary: A list of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to their product information has been published.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must review the changes to update their product dossiers and ensure compliance with the new safety information.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: The authority provides guidance on the end‑of‑year submission dates for type I variations in 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams with marketing authorisation holders who expect an outcome in 2026 must plan to submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super‑groupings by the specified dates.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: EMA Management Board: highlights of September 2026 meeting
entries.description: Mid-year report 2026 from the Executive DirectorEMA presented results and achievements of its operations for the first half of 2026 to the Management Board. Between January and…
entries.summary: EMA presented the mid‑year results and achievements of its operations for the first half of 2026 to the Management Board.
entries.why_it_matters: The report provides an overview of EMA’s performance but does not introduce new regulatory changes, so RA teams should monitor for future updates.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: EMA endorses ICMRA joint statement urging advancement of animal‑testing alternatives throughout the medicine lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across all therapeutic areas must be aware that regulators are increasingly encouraging non‑animal data, potentially impacting study designs, submissions and compliance strategies.

entries.description: Amsterdam, 28 September 2026Check against delivery (The published text is based on the prepared speech. Minor differences may have occurred during delivery)Good morning,…
entries.summary: No substantive regulatory change was announced in the speech.
entries.why_it_matters: This update does not alter regulatory requirements for RA teams.

entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change

But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…
entries.summary: EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap by the end of 2026 to address women’s health considerations in medicines development and regulation.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor the forthcoming roadmap to ensure future submissions incorporate women‑specific data and considerations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: The register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware of the updated list to ensure accurate tracking of supplementary protection certificates for the drugs they manage.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states contact points are designated to review the national implementation of quick response codes for veterinary medicinal products authorised through the centralised, mutual recognition, decentralised and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that contact points are available for reviewing QR code implementation across all procedures and should use them for any compliance or audit questions.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP
entries.description: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP
entries.summary: A new procedure (INS‑GCP‑1) has been issued for coordinating good‑clinical‑practice inspections requested by the CHMP.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware of the updated inspection coordination process to ensure timely and compliant responses to CHMP inspection requests.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list
entries.description: This is a list of certain generic drug submissions currently under review. The Generic Submissions Under Review list includes the medicinal ingredient(s) and therapeutic area. Downloadable Excel files are included.
entries.summary: The FDA released a monthly list of generic drug submissions currently under review.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should monitor the list to stay informed about which generic submissions are in review and adjust their timelines accordingly.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.description: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.summary: Certain substances are now excluded from the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 regarding residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling veterinary medicinal products must monitor which substances are excluded to adjust residue monitoring and compliance activities accordingly.

entries.label: MHRA
entries.title: Unlock the MHRA Regulatory Advice Service for Medical Devices

entries.summary: The MHRA launched a new Regulatory Advice Service for medical devices to provide direct support to developers.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams can now schedule consultations with MHRA to clarify device requirements and streamline compliance.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.description: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.summary: New pharmacovigilance recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products have been issued.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for veterinary products must update their pharmacovigilance processes to comply with the new guidance.

entries.title: Draft guideline on veterinary good pharmacovigilance practices (VGVP) Module: Signal Management - Revision 1

entries.summary: This draft guideline updates signal management practices for veterinary pharmacovigilance.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams in veterinary pharmacovigilance must review the revised signal management procedures to align future submissions.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Compliance and enforcement policy for health products (POL-0001)
entries.description: This policy describes Health Canada's national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
entries.summary: Health Canada releases a policy outlining its national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: All RA teams responsible for health products must align their compliance procedures with the new national enforcement approach.
